docs.title: Dotfiles Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for my chezmoi-powered cross-platform dotfiles.

This site provides a deeper, structured explanation of how the repository works, how to customize it, and how scripts, templates, themes, and configuration files fit together.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This project uses chezmoi to manage configurations for:

  • Windows
  • macOS
  • Linux, with first-class Omarchy support (plain Arch, Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora also work)

The dotfiles are structured to be idempotent, portable, templatized, and data-driven.

docs.text:
To install these dotfiles, run the installer appropriate for your platform:

{%
    include-markdown "../../README.md"
    start="## Quick Start"

docs.title: Documentation Sections
docs.text:
• Scripts: automation scripts in .chezmoiscripts/
  • Templates: reusable components in .chezmoitemplates/
  • Configuration: how data in .chezmoidata/ drives the dotfiles, including per-distro Linux packages
  • AI Tools: MCP servers, plugins, skills and packages for AI agents
  • Themes: how the theme system works
  • Omarchy: what Omarchy owns and what chezmoi manages on top of it

docs.title: Source Code
docs.text:
All files referenced in this documentation exist in the GitHub repo. You can explore them directly here:

👉 https://github.com/Stackclash/dotfiles

docs.title: AI Tools (ai-tools.yaml)
docs.text:
A data-driven workflow for adding and managing AI developer tools — MCP servers, plugins, skills, agents, and package-manager CLIs — across any number of AI coding agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, …), the same way apps.yaml manages applications.

Two files drive it:

File Answers home/.chezmoidata/ai-tools.yaml What to install: MCP servers, plugins, skills, packages home/.chezmoidata/ai-agents.yaml How each agent receives things: its CLI, how MCP servers reach it, where skills go

Edit those files and run chezmoi apply — nothing else needs touching.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
chezmoi apply does everything, in two ways:

Mechanism Handles chezmoi templates package tools and agent CLIs → mise config (~/.config/mise/config.toml); vscode-json agents' MCP servers → VS Code mcp.json (next to settings.json) run_onchange_after_04-sync-ai-tools script (per-OS: PowerShell + bash) imperative installs: MCP registration, plugin installs, published skill installs (npx skills add), custom skill/agent copy, package post-install steps

The sync script inlines the tool list from ai-tools.yaml at render time, so it always reflects the current data. Every external command it runs is best-effort: if a CLI (claude, codex, …) isn't installed yet, it logs a follow-up note and moves on — a missing tool never fails chezmoi apply.

docs.title: Agents (ai-agents.yaml)
docs.text:
One entry per agent. The sync script and templates never name an agent; they loop over this registry, so adding an agent is one new entry — no script edits for any agent whose needs fit the existing options below.

aiAgents:
  codex:
    displayName: OpenAI Codex
    cli: codex                      # binary probed before CLI-based installs
    install:                        # optional: install the CLI itself via mise
      mise: { tool: codex }         # registry short name (same key Omarchy uses);
                                    # or { backend: npm, package: "@openai/codex" }
    mcp:
      method: codex-toml            # claude-cli | vscode-json | codex-toml | none
      file: .codex/config.toml      # (codex-toml) relative to $HOME
    plugins:
      supported: false              # has `<cli> plugin marketplace add` / `plugin install`?
    skills:
      cliAgent: codex               # `npx skills add --agent <this>` ("" = unsupported)
      dir: .codex/skills            # custom skills are copied here (relative to $HOME)
      agentsDir: ""                 # custom agents are copied here ("" = none)
      manifest: ""                  # optional skills manifest to update (relative to $HOME)
mcp.method What happens claude-cli claude mcp add-json --scope user (best-effort; skipped if the CLI is missing) vscode-json the server is written to the managed VS Code mcp.json (Copilot reads it from there) codex-toml the servers are rendered as [mcp_servers.<name>] tables inside a marker-delimited block (# BEGIN/END chezmoi ai-tools mcp) in mcp.file. Everything else in that file — Codex stores trust levels there — is left alone. type is dropped and headers becomes http_headers. none the agent receives no MCP servers from here

Define an MCP server in a way the existing methods can't express (a different config format, say) by adding one branch for the new mcp.method in each of the two sync scripts and a rendering template if needed — everything else stays data.

docs.title: Adding an agent
docs.text:
1. Add its entry to ai-agents.yaml.
  2. Run chezmoi apply. Every tool in ai-tools.yaml with no agents: list now targets it automatically, and its CLI is installed if install: is set.
  3. Optional: a plugin entry gains support by declaring a subkey named after the agent (and the agent needs plugins.supported: true).

A misspelled agent name in an agents: list fails the render with the list of valid names, rather than silently installing nowhere.

docs.title: The schema
docs.text:
aiTools is organized by category — the key under aiTools tells you what a tool is; there is no separate type: field.

aiTools:
  mcp:     { <name>: {...} }
  plugin:  { <name>: {...} }
  skill:   { <name>: {...} }
  package: { <name>: {...} }
  custom:  { <name>: {...} }

Every entry may set forPersonal: false to skip it on work machines. mcp, skill and custom entries may set agents: [claude, codex] to limit which agents (keys of ai-agents.yaml) receive them; omit it to target every agent, including ones added later. plugin entries target an agent by declaring a subkey named after it; package entries have no per-agent behavior. Neither plugin nor package entries carry agents.

docs.title: mcp — MCP servers
docs.text:
Delivered to each targeted agent by that agent's mcp.method (see Agents). A single config: dict, written in the Claude/VS Code JSON shape, is the one source for all of them — any field those schemas support just works, and the codex-toml method translates it for Codex.

  mcp:
    playwright-mcp:
      config:
        type: stdio
        command: npx
        args: ["@playwright/mcp@latest"]

    context7:
      config:
        type: http
        url: "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp"
        headers:
          CONTEXT7_API_KEY: "{{ (dopplerProjectJson \"dotfiles\" \"prd\").CONTEXT7_API_KEY }}"

Secrets: any string inside config: containing {{ is executed as a real chezmoi template (via chezmoi execute-template) before being embedded in the rendered JSON — not simple {{ .key }} substitution, so any chezmoi template function works, including Doppler's. The Doppler CLI is already mise-managed (github:DopplerHQ/cli); authenticate it once per machine (doppler login, doppler setup) and reference secrets with {{ (dopplerProjectJson "<project>" "<config>").<SECRET_NAME> }}. Remove a headers/env entry entirely to run a server keyless.

docs.title: package — package-manager CLIs
docs.text:
No agents field — package installs aren't per-agent:

  package:
    graphify:
      mise: { backend: pipx, package: graphifyy }
      postInstall: "graphify install"

docs.title: plugin — marketplace plugins
docs.text:
A plugin installs for whichever agents it declares a subkey for (and only agents with plugins.supported: true):

  plugin:
    superpowers:
      claude:  { marketplaceAdd: "anthropics/claude-plugins-official", install: "superpowers@claude-plugins-official" }
      copilot: { marketplaceAdd: "obra/superpowers-marketplace", install: "superpowers@superpowers-marketplace" }

docs.title: skill — published skills from a GitHub repo
docs.text:
Installed with the skills CLI, the package manager for agent skills:

npx --yes skills add <repo> [--skill <skill>] --agent <skills.cliAgent> -g -y

  skill:
    brainstorming:
      # agents: [claude, codex]  # optional -- omit for every agent
      repo: obra/superpowers    # <owner>/<repo> on GitHub
      skill: brainstorming      # optional -- omit to install every skill in the repo
Field Required Meaning repo yes <owner>/<repo> to install from skill no a single skill inside that repo; omit to take them all agents no limit to these agents; default is all. Each agent's skills.cliAgent is the --agent value (claude-code, github-copilot, codex, …)

The sync script runs one npx skills add per targeted agent, always with -g (user-level, so the skill applies to every project) and -y (no prompts, so chezmoi apply never blocks). If npx is missing or an install fails, the exact command is printed as a follow-up note instead of failing the apply.

Use this for skills someone else publishes; use custom below for skills you write yourself.

docs.title: custom — your own skills and agents
docs.text:
custom:
    my-skill:
      kind: skill        # skill | agent
      # agents: [claude, codex]  # optional -- omit for every agent

Author the content once under the neutral source directory, then declare it:

home/dot_ai/skills/<name>/SKILL.md     ->  ~/.ai/skills/<name>/
home/dot_ai/agents/<name>/             ->  ~/.ai/agents/<name>/

The sync script copies it into each targeted agent's location (copy, not symlink — so it works on Windows without Developer Mode). The destination comes from the agent's skills.dir (skills) or skills.agentsDir (agents); an agent with an empty agentsDir simply skips agents. Today:

kind Claude Copilot Codex skill ~/.claude/skills/<name> ~/.agents/skills/<name> (+ registered in its skills manifest if present) ~/.codex/skills/<name> agent ~/.claude/agents/<name> — (Copilot agents are extension-defined) —

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
chezmoi apply    # renders configs + runs the sync when ai-tools.yaml changes

To force a re-sync without changing the data (e.g. to pick up latest plugin/package versions), re-run all onchange scripts:

chezmoi apply --force

Verify:

claude mcp list          # playwright + context7 registered
mise ls                  # graphifyy + @fission-ai/openspec present
codex mcp list           # Codex servers from the managed block
ls ~/.claude/skills ~/.agents/skills ~/.codex/skills  # installed + custom skills present

docs.title: Removing tools
docs.text:
Delete an entry from ai-tools.yaml and run chezmoi apply: the sync script uninstalls what it previously installed and no longer finds in the data. It covers Claude MCP servers, plugins, skills and custom skills/agents; package entries are not removed (use mise uninstall).

How it works: each run records every tool it targets as a type|agent-or-method|name|extra line in ~/.local/state/chezmoi-ai-tools.state. Lines missing from the next run are removed (claude mcp remove, <cli> plugin uninstall, npx skills remove, or deleting the copied custom directory). A removal that fails stays in the file and is retried on the next apply.

  • Only tools this script installed are touched. Anything you added by hand is left alone.
  • The first run after upgrading has no state file, so it removes nothing and just starts tracking.
  • Narrowing an entry's agents: list also removes it from the dropped agents.
  • Skills with no skill: field (whole-repo installs) are not tracked, because their names are unknown.
  • Plugin marketplaces are not removed; run <cli> plugin marketplace remove <name> yourself.
  • Codex and Copilot MCP servers need no tracking: their config is regenerated on every apply.

docs.title: Starter tools
docs.text: Tool Type Agents Notes playwright-mcp mcp all browser automation context7 mcp all docs lookup; optional API key github mcp all GitHub API; needs a PAT superpowers plugin claude, copilot skills/workflow bundle (Codex: no plugin support yet) vercel-react-best-practices skill all from vercel-labs/agent-skills web-design-guidelines skill all from vercel-labs/agent-skills graphify package (pipx) — graphify install post-step openspec package (npm) — per-repo openspec init

docs.title: Invalid configuration: : Invalid input when registering an MCP
docs.text:
Fixed — but worth knowing why, because it will bite any new PowerShell code that passes JSON to a native command. Windows PowerShell reconstructs a command line from the argument strings and does not escape embedded double quotes, so {"type":"stdio"} reached claude as {type:stdio} (and any config with a space in it — a Bearer <token> header — was split into several arguments). claude mcp add-json then failed schema validation on the garbage it parsed.

The Windows sync script routes JSON through ConvertTo-NativeArg, which escapes to the CommandLineToArgvW rules. PowerShell 7.3+ handles this natively via $PSNativeCommandArgumentPassing, except in its default Windows mode when the target is a .cmd/.bat shim — which is exactly how npm-installed CLIs land on PATH — so the helper checks both before deciding to escape.

docs.title: An MCP is skipped for rendering <no value>
docs.text:
A {{ ... }} expression inside config: resolved to nothing — nearly always a Doppler secret that doesn't exist under the name given, since missingkey=zero turns a missing key into the literal text <no value>. Check what the config actually renders to:

chezmoi execute-template '{{ includeTemplate "mcp-server-json" .aiTools.mcp.github.config }}'

Fix the secret name (or add the secret in Doppler) and re-run chezmoi apply --force.

The sync script refuses to register a server in this state. That guard matters more than it looks on Windows: < and > are cmd.exe redirection operators, so an unresolved value doesn't just store a broken server — it corrupts the command line on the way to a .cmd-shimmed claude, which surfaces as the same Invalid configuration: : Invalid input described above. The same hazard applies to any secret containing &, |, ^, < or >; if you hit that, configure the server in ~/.claude.json directly rather than through the CLI.

docs.title: No matching skills found for: <name>
docs.text: The skill: key must be the published skill name exactly; the CLI does not fuzzy-match. Run npx --yes skills add <owner>/<repo> with no --skill to list what the repo actually offers, then copy the name verbatim. (Vercel's skills are all vercel--prefixed: vercel-react-best-practices, not react-best-practices.)

docs.title: Failed to install plugin: Access is denied. (os error 5)
docs.text:
A known Copilot CLI bug on Windows: the installer swaps the installed-plugins folder, and Windows refuses to replace a directory while VS Code's Copilot extension or a live copilot session holds watcher handles on it. Close VS Code and any running copilot session, then:

chezmoi apply --force

docs.title: Archon code-task workflow
docs.text:
An interactive Archon workflow for general coding tasks. It takes a change from requirements to a validated, reviewed result on its own branch:

  1. Gather requirements from an Azure DevOps work item or an interview.
  2. Plan the work, with independent review and your approval.
  3. Build test-first, one task at a time.
  4. Validate with four separate reviews and verification steps.
  5. Write the glossary, ADRs, and a report, and optionally open a draft PR.

It pauses at gates for your decisions, so it runs in the foreground.

The workflow is generic. It discovers each repository's own test, lint, build, and typecheck commands instead of assuming a toolchain.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
Source (this repo) Deployed to home/dot_archon/workflows/dev/code-task/code-task.yaml.tmpl ~/.archon/workflows/dev/code-task/code-task.yaml home/dot_archon/workflows/dev/code-task/commands/*.md AI prompts, one per AI node home/dot_archon/workflows/dev/code-task/scripts/*.ts Deterministic gates and glue (Bun) home/dot_archon/workflows/dev/code-task/fixtures/*.stubs.yaml Dry-run fixtures home/dot_archon/workflows/dev/dot_shared/*.ts Pack-level shared modules (.shared/)

The YAML is a chezmoi template only so that it can read one value: the default Azure DevOps project, from the AZURE_PROJECT secret in Doppler (project personal, config default). This is the same way the azure-ado MCP server gets AZURE_ORG. Leave the secret unset if you don't use Azure DevOps; the default is then empty.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
archon workflow run code-task --branch my-change "Add retry to the uploader"

With an Azure DevOps work item:

archon workflow run code-task --branch task-4521 "AB#4521"

Interactive workflows refuse --detach on a fresh launch. Run it in the foreground (or as a background task of your harness), then answer each gate with archon workflow approve.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Purpose work_item "" ADO work item ID (1234) or URL. Overrides any reference in the message. ado_project Doppler AZURE_PROJECT ADO project for bare IDs and AB# references. projects_dir chezmoi projectPath Folder holding your local projects. Agents look for other repos here, and are told never to search the whole filesystem, which can hang a run.

docs.title: Work item references
docs.text:
Archon checks these in order. The first match wins:

  1. --input work_item=1234, or --input work_item=<work item URL>
  2. A work item URL in the message: https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_workitems/edit/1234 or https://{org}.visualstudio.com/{project}/_workitems/edit/1234
  3. AB#1234 in the message

A bare #1234 is not treated as a work item, so "fix the bug from #12" is never misread.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• archon and bun on PATH (both managed through mise).
  • The Claude provider. The ADO fetch and the PR step use Claude's user-level MCP servers.
  • Optional: the azure-ado MCP server from ai-tools.yaml. If it's missing or disconnected, the workflow falls back to the interview and says why.
  • The gh CLI, only if you want draft PRs opened on GitHub.

docs.title: The nodes
docs.text:
The run moves through five stages. Each stage has its own chart below. In every chart, blue is an AI node, grey is a deterministic script, and an amber hexagon is a gate where you decide. A box labelled loop repeats as a unit (an Archon loop_group).

flowchart TD
    classDef stage fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111827
    classDef gate fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f

    R["1. Requirements<br/>ticket or interview<br/>→ proposal.md"]:::stage
    P["2. Planning<br/>baseline, plan, review<br/>→ plan.md"]:::stage
    PA{{"plan-approval"}}:::gate
    CM{{"commit-mode"}}:::gate
    B["3. Build<br/>test-first, per task"]:::stage
    V["4. Validation<br/>checks, 4 reviews,<br/>verification"]:::stage
    FG{{"findings-gate"}}:::gate
    C["5. Close-out<br/>docs, report, PR"]:::stage

    R --> P --> PA --> CM --> B --> V --> FG --> C
    PA -. "Back to interview" .-> P
    FG -. "Fix" .-> V

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Every path ends in one proposal.md, the single brief the rest of the run works from. This stage is read-only.

flowchart TD
    classDef ai fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
    classDef script fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111827
    classDef gate fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f

    intake["intake"]:::script
    fetch["fetch-ado"]:::ai
    checkfetch["check-fetch<br/>(fails run on bad fetch)"]:::script
    reconcile["reconcile-ticket"]:::ai
    ready["ticket-ready"]:::script
    subgraph INT["interview (loop)"]
        iround["interview-round"]:::ai --> igate{{"interview-gate<br/>Send answers / Ready"}}:::gate
    end
    writeprop["write-proposal"]:::ai
    fromticket["proposal-from-ticket"]:::ai
    checkprop["check-proposal"]:::script

    intake -- "work item + MCP connected" --> fetch --> checkfetch --> reconcile --> ready
    intake -- "no work item, or fallback" --> INT
    ready -- "gaps or conflicts" --> INT
    ready -- "complete" --> fromticket
    INT --> writeprop --> checkprop
    fromticket --> checkprop
Node Type What it does intake script Parses the work item reference and resolves the ADO project. Probes claude mcp get azure-ado. Routes to ado or interview; a failed probe or a missing project falls back to the interview with a stated reason. fetch-ado AI (small, read-only ADO tools) Transcribes the work item, its parent and children, related titles, and the last 20 comments into work-item.md. Reports gaps. check-fetch script Fails the run if the fetch failed (not found, auth, wrong org). Writes ticket-gaps.md. reconcile-ticket AI Checks the ticket against the code, the context files, the glossary, and the ADRs. Reports only conflicts it can cite on both sides. ticket-ready script complete = no gaps and no conflicts. interview loop Grilling-style rounds: the frontier of open decisions, each with a recommended answer. Starts with read-only recon of the context files, glossary, and ADRs. In ticket-review mode it confirms each acceptance criterion, then the gaps, then the conflicts. Ends only when you choose Ready. write-proposal / proposal-from-ticket AI Write proposal.md: acceptance criteria as ### AC-n GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios, invariants, goals and non-goals, decisions, glossary and ADR candidates. check-proposal script Validates the AC format and unique IDs, and that the worktree is unchanged.

docs.title: 2. Planning
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    classDef ai fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
    classDef script fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111827
    classDef gate fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f

    tool["discover-toolchain"]:::ai --> base["baseline"]:::script --> prep
    subgraph PLOOP["planning (loop until Approve plan)"]
        prep["prepare-clarify"]:::script
        subgraph CLAR["clarify (loop)"]
            cround["clarify-round"]:::ai --> cgate{{"clarify-gate<br/>Send answers / Ready"}}:::gate
        end
        revprop["revise-proposal"]:::ai --> recheck["recheck-proposal"]:::script
        plan["plan"]:::ai --> checkplan["check-plan"]:::script
        subgraph REV["plan-review (loop, max 3)"]
            rplan["review-plan"]:::ai --> revplan["revise-plan"]:::ai --> rround["review-round"]:::script
        end
        fcheck["final-check-plan"]:::script --> summary["gate-summary"]:::script
        papprove{{"plan-approval<br/>Approve / Revise plan /<br/>Back to interview"}}:::gate

        prep -- "issues or Back to interview" --> CLAR --> revprop
        prep -- "first pass or Revise plan" --> plan
        recheck --> plan
        checkplan -- "no proposal issues" --> REV --> fcheck
        summary --> papprove
        checkplan -. "proposal issues: next pass" .-> prep
        papprove -. "not approved: next pass" .-> prep
    end
Node Type What it does discover-toolchain AI (small, read-only) Finds the repo's declared test, lint, build, and typecheck commands, plus has_tests. Never invents a command. baseline script Runs those commands on the untouched branch. Pre-existing failures are recorded, not fatal; later stages judge only new failures. planning loop One pass: clarify (only when reopened), plan, check-plan, review, and your approval. Repeats until you choose Approve plan. plan AI (large) One task per test-first cycle (### T-n), each with Files, Satisfies (AC-n), Tests (or Verification steps when the repo has no tests), Depends on, and Done when. Blocking problems go under ## Proposal issues. check-plan script Every AC is covered, references are valid, required fields are present. Proposal issues send the next pass back to clarification. plan-review loop (max 3) An independent fresh-context reviewer, plus a reviser. After 3 rounds it hands open findings to your gate instead of failing. plan-approval gate Approve plan / Revise plan (your text is feedback) / Back to interview.

docs.title: 3. Build
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    classDef ai fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
    classDef script fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111827
    classDef gate fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f

    cmode{{"commit-mode<br/>Each task / At end / Don't commit"}}:::gate --> next
    subgraph BLOOP["build (loop per task attempt, until all tasks done)"]
        next["next-task"]:::script
        wtests["write-tests"]:::ai
        red["red-check<br/>(tests must fail)"]:::script
        subgraph IMPL["implement-task (loop, max 3 attempts)"]
            impl["implement"]:::ai --> green["green-check<br/>(tests pass, unchanged)"]:::script
            green -- "check red at baseline" --> rjudge["regression-judge"]:::ai --> verdict["green-verdict"]:::script
            green -- "otherwise" --> verdict
        end
        finish["finish-task"]:::script
        stucks["stuck-summary"]:::script
        sgate{{"stuck-gate<br/>Retry / I fixed it / Abort"}}:::gate

        next -- "repo has tests" --> wtests --> red
        next -- "no tests, or tests already red" --> red
        red -- "ready" --> IMPL --> finish
        red -- "red check failed" --> finish
        finish -- "task not done" --> stucks --> sgate
        sgate -. "next pass" .-> next
    end
Node Type What it does commit-mode gate Asked once, before any code: Commit after each task / Commit once at the end / Don't commit. next-task script Picks the next task in dependency order, carries stuck-gate guidance forward, and acts on Abort. write-tests AI Writes only the task's tests and declares a targeted test command. red-check script Only the declared test files changed, and the targeted tests fail. Records the test file hashes. implement-task loop (max 3) implement (AI), then green-check: the targeted tests pass with the test files unchanged; checks that passed at baseline still pass; checks that failed at baseline go to regression-judge (AI), which compares the logs. finish-task script Marks the task done and commits it if per-task commits were chosen. stuck-gate gate After 3 failed attempts, or a red check that couldn't be satisfied: Retry with guidance / I fixed it, re-check / Abort run.

Repos without tests skip the test steps. Lint, build, and typecheck still run after every task.

docs.title: 4. Validation
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    classDef ai fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
    classDef script fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111827
    classDef gate fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f

    subgraph VAL["validation (loop until clean or Accept as-is)"]
        vstart["validation-start"]:::script
        fixes["apply-fixes"]:::ai --> cfix["commit-fixes"]:::script
        fchecks["final-checks"]:::script
        fjudge["final-judge"]:::ai
        racc["review-acceptance"]:::ai
        rqual["review-quality"]:::ai
        rsec["review-security"]:::ai
        rerr["review-errors"]:::ai
        vsetup["verification-setup"]:::script
        vprep["prepare-verification"]:::ai
        subgraph VER["verification (loop until every step has a result)"]
            vrec["record-verification"]:::ai --> vstat["verification-status"]:::script --> vgate{{"verify-gate<br/>Run these scripts /<br/>My manual results"}}:::gate
        end
        fsum["findings-summary"]:::script
        fgate{{"findings-gate<br/>Fix / Accept as-is / Abort"}}:::gate

        vstart -- "Fix chosen" --> fixes
        vstart --> fchecks
        cfix --> fchecks
        fchecks -- "check red at baseline" --> fjudge
        fchecks --> racc & rqual & rsec & rerr
        fjudge --> racc
        racc --> vsetup -- "no tests, or uncovered behavior" --> vprep --> VER
        VER --> fsum
        rqual & rsec & rerr --> fsum
        fsum -- "findings" --> fgate
        fgate -. "next pass" .-> vstart
    end
Node Type What it does validation-start script Acts on the previous findings gate: records Fix direction, or ends the run on Abort. apply-fixes / commit-fixes AI / script Fix only what you chose. Committed if you chose per-task commits. final-checks (+ final-judge) script (+ AI) Every check over the whole change, against the baseline. Also fails if any proven-failing test was edited. review-acceptance AI (large) Traces each AC-n to evidence, checks invariants and scope, and lists behavior no test covers. review-quality AI Fit with conventions, reuse, simplicity, clarity, test quality. review-security AI (large) Injection, secrets, authorization, input validation, unsafe defaults, dependencies, data exposure. review-errors AI Swallowed errors, propagation, failure paths, edge cases, resource cleanup. verification loop For repos without tests, and for behavior no test covers. Each step has manual instructions and, where possible, an explained script. Nothing runs unless you ask. Passed steps keep their result across fix passes. findings-gate gate Findings grouped by review: Fix (optionally say which) / Accept as-is / Abort run. It also flags verified steps whose files a fix touched.

The four reviews run in parallel, each from its own command file (review-*.md), so you can tune each one independently.

docs.title: 5. Close-out
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    classDef ai fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
    classDef script fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#111827
    classDef gate fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f

    cend["commit-end"]:::script --> dstart["docs-start"]:::script --> wdocs["write-docs"]:::ai --> cdocs["check-docs"]:::script
    cdocs --> wreport["write-report"]:::ai --> creport["check-report"]:::script --> prc["pr-check"]:::script
    prc -- "branch has commits" --> pgate{{"pr-gate<br/>Open a draft PR / Don't"}}:::gate --> pdec["pr-decision"]:::script
    pdec -- "open" --> openpr["open-pr"]:::ai
Node Type What it does commit-end script The single commit, if you chose Commit once at the end. It runs after validation, so it includes the fixes. write-docs + check-docs AI + script Updates $DOCS_DIR/GLOSSARY.md and writes ADRs to $DOCS_DIR/adr/. The AI decides what qualifies as an ADR: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and a real trade-off. Confined to $DOCS_DIR and never committed. write-report + check-report AI + script report.md: summary, every AC with its evidence, tests added, checks, verification, accepted findings, commits, docs, and branch. pr-check / pr-gate / open-pr script / gate / AI Only when the branch has commits: Open a draft PR / Don't open a PR. Opening one pushes the branch. Supports GitHub (gh) and Azure DevOps (ADO MCP).

docs.title: Gates you'll see
docs.text: Gate When Choices interview-gate Each interview round Send answers / Ready: write proposal clarify-gate When planning reopens requirements Send answers / Ready: update proposal plan-approval Each planning pass without proposal issues Approve plan / Revise plan / Back to interview commit-mode Once, before building Commit after each task / Commit once at the end / Don't commit stuck-gate A task that can't be completed Retry with guidance / I fixed it, re-check / Abort run verify-gate Pending verification steps Run these scripts (step IDs or all) / Here are my manual results findings-gate Validation found something Fix / Accept as-is / Abort run pr-gate The branch has commits Open a draft PR / Don't open a PR

docs.title: Guarantees enforced in code
docs.text:
These checks are scripts, not AI judgment:

  • Requirements gathering and planning never change the worktree.
  • A failed ADO fetch fails the run. It is never silently replaced.
  • Every acceptance criterion has an ID, GIVEN/WHEN/THEN lines, and at least one planned task.
  • A task's tests are written before its code, touch only test files, and fail before implementation.
  • An implementation passes only with its proven-failing tests unchanged.
  • Checks that passed at baseline must keep passing. Pre-existing failures never count against the change.
  • Commits never include $DOCS_DIR or files left behind by the baseline.
  • The workflow never writes to the Azure DevOps board. The PR description names the work item in plain text, not with AB#.
  • The run always works in its own worktree (worktree.enabled: true).

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
Everything lands in the run's $ARTIFACTS_DIR:

File Produced by work-item.md, ticket-gaps.md, ticket-conflicts.md ADO path interview-notes.md, clarify-notes.md Interview and clarification rounds proposal.md The brief; the contract for the whole run baseline.md, baseline-<check>.log Baseline run plan.md, plan-review.md Planning build-state.json, current-task.md, green-report.md, *.log Build and validation checks findings.md, verification.md Validation report.md Final report (also the workflow's returned output)

docs.title: Customizing
docs.text:
Prompts. Edit commands/<node>.md. The review prompts are separate on purpose, so you can tighten quality, security, or error handling on its own.

Gates and wiring. Edit code-task.yaml.tmpl. Load errors show up in:

archon workflow list

The 18 fixtures cover every routing branch without AI spend:

archon workflow test code-task

Method credits. The interview adapts grilling and domain-modeling from mattpocock/skills (MIT) and brainstorming from obra/superpowers. The text is vendored, so behavior is pinned to this repo rather than to whatever skill versions are installed.

Engineering discipline. The planning, test-writing, implementation, fix, and review prompts carry a paraphrased form of the guidelines in multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills:

Guideline Where it lives Think before coding: state assumptions, don't pick an interpretation silently, push back on needless complexity interview and clarify put interpretations to you as questions. plan records an ## Assumptions section, which the plan-approval gate shows you. write-tests, implement, and apply-fixes state their assumptions in their output or in test comments, since they run unattended. Simplicity first: minimum code, nothing speculative plan, revise-plan, implement, apply-fixes, write-tests; checked by review-plan and review-quality. review-errors will not ask for handling of impossible scenarios. Surgical changes: every changed line traces to the task plan (no cleanup tasks), implement, apply-fixes, write-tests; checked by review-plan and review-quality. Goal-driven execution: verifiable success criteria Built into the workflow: test-first tasks with Done when conditions, deterministic red and green checks. implement also lists its edits with the check that proves each one before starting.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Dry runs evaluate each loop once. Fixtures prove routing within a pass, but second passes (interview rounds, a planning bounce, a stuck-gate retry, validation fix passes) are proven only by real runs.
  • Two load warnings on stuck-gate and verify-gate are expected. Their answers are acted on by the next pass (next-task, record-verification) rather than by the loop's exit check, so Retry and Re-check can continue the loop.
  • Abort ends the run as failed with an explicit message. Archon requires a loop's gate to be its last node, so a cancel step can't follow it.
  • The prompts are a first version. Refine them from what real runs show.

docs.title: Configuration Data (.chezmoidata + .chezmoi.json.tmpl)
docs.text:
Every dynamic setting lives in YAML under home/.chezmoidata/. Templates and scripts read each file's top-level key (for example .apps). Edit a file and run chezmoi apply: the run_onchange_* scripts embed a hash of the data they read, so they re-run on their own.

home/.chezmoidata/
├── apps.yaml                     # .apps
├── linux-package-managers.yaml   # .linuxPackageManagers
├── omarchy.yaml                  # .omarchyPrefs
├── ai-tools.yaml                 # .aiTools   (see AI Tools)
├── ai-agents.yaml                # .aiAgents  (see AI Tools)
├── themes.yaml                   # .themes    (see Themes)
└── vscode-profiles.yaml          # .vscodeProfiles

docs.title: apps.yaml
docs.text:
One entry per app, with a block for each OS it installs on. An app with no block for an OS is skipped there. forPersonal: true skips the app on work machines.

apps:
  vscode:
    forPersonal: false
    windows: { id: "Microsoft.VisualStudioCode", method: winget }   # winget | choco
    darwin:  { id: "visual-studio-code", method: brew-cask }       # brew | brew-cask | brew-tap
    linux:
      omarchy: { installer: editor-vscode, package: visual-studio-code-bin }
      aur: visual-studio-code-bin

The linux: block maps each package manager to a package name. The install script uses the first manager in this distro's list (below) that the app defines. omarchy: takes one of:

  • shipped: Omarchy already provides the app, so nothing runs
  • { installer, package }: runs omarchy-install-<installer> only when <package> is missing. Those installers also configure and launch the app.

Important

apps.yaml holds only what mise can't manage: apps with no mise build, or ones that need the OS package (Docker CLI plugins, syncthing's systemd unit, PowerShell as a system shell). Everything mise can install goes in dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl.

Omarchy's base apps that mise can't install (chromium, mpv, localsend, …) are listed as omarchy: shipped plus pacman/apt/dnf names, so any other Linux machine gets the same setup.

docs.title: Omarchy and the mise config
docs.text:
Omarchy also ships CLI tools of its own:

  • Through pacman: bat, eza, fzf, ripgrep, zoxide, lazygit, neovim, starship and others. The mise config puts these in an {{ if not (includeTemplate "is-omarchy" .) }} block, so they're installed everywhere except Omarchy.
  • Through mise itself (/etc/mise/conf.d/omarchy-tools.toml): gh, copilot, codex, node, uv and others, installed lazily and auto-updated. The mise template reads that file when it exists and skips any unpinned ("latest") entry Omarchy already declares, so Omarchy stays in charge and nothing installs twice. Pinned entries such as node = "22" still apply. Declare these with their registry short names (gh, not github:cli/cli) so the keys match.

When a tool has no build for every OS, limit it with mise's os option, for example tmux = { version = "latest", os = ["linux", "macos"] }.

docs.title: linux-package-managers.yaml
docs.text:
The package managers to try for each distro, keyed by /etc/os-release ID:

linuxPackageManagers:
  omarchy: [omarchy, pacman, aur]
  arch: [pacman, aur]
  debian: [apt]
  fedora: [dnf]

The script matches .chezmoi.osRelease.id first, then each word of .chezmoi.osRelease.idLike, so Manjaro uses arch and Ubuntu uses debian. On Omarchy, pacman/aur go through omarchy-pkg-add / omarchy-pkg-aur-add. Elsewhere they use pacman/yay (or paru). apt and dnf use install -y.

To override the list on one machine, add it to ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.json:

{ "data": { "packageManagers": ["pacman", "aur"] } }

Adding a distro takes one entry. Adding a new manager also needs one case branch in install_with (and upgrade_with) in Linux/run_02-install-apps.sh.tmpl.

docs.title: omarchy.yaml
docs.text: Omarchy desktop preferences, applied only on Omarchy. See Omarchy.

docs.title: vscode-profiles.yaml
docs.text: common_extensions go into base VS Code and every profile. profiles.<name>.extensions are added per profile. Synced by the run_03-setup-vscode-profiles scripts.

docs.title: .chezmoi.json.tmpl: machine variables
docs.text:
Prompts asked once on chezmoi init, stored in ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.json:

Variable Description .name, .email Identity .workComputer Skips forPersonal apps and enables work-repo cloning .setupWork Only asked when workComputer is false. Enables work identity and work-repo cloning without skipping forPersonal apps .workEmail, .workGithubOrg Only asked when workComputer or setupWork is true .githubUsername, .projectPath Repo cloning .context7ApiKey Optional MCP key .theme Theme from themes.yaml (Windows Terminal / VS Code)

To change an answer later, edit ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.json, or run chezmoi init --prompt to be asked every question again.

docs.title: OS detection
docs.text:
Use chezmoi's built-in data, not custom flags:

{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" }}...{{ end }}                  {{/* windows | darwin | linux */}}
{{ if includeTemplate "is-omarchy" . }}...{{ end }}         {{/* Omarchy only */}}

.chezmoi.osRelease only exists on Linux. The is-omarchy template checks .chezmoi.os first, then .chezmoi.osRelease.id == "omarchy".

docs.title: Omarchy
docs.text: Omarchy is an Arch + Hyprland setup that ships its own defaults under /usr/share/omarchy ($OMARCHY_PATH) and copies user-editable files into ~/.config. These dotfiles sit on top of Omarchy without fighting it: Omarchy keeps its defaults, and chezmoi only adds your changes.

docs.title: What Omarchy owns vs. what chezmoi manages
docs.text:
Area Omarchy provides chezmoi does ~/.bashrc env-bootstrap + $OMARCHY_PATH/default/bash/rc (aliases, mise, starship, zoxide, fzf) Keeps both source lines and adds only gh/kubectl completions ~/.profile, zsh Login PATH via env-bootstrap (mise command-wrappers first, shims last) Not deployed on Omarchy Prompt Starship + ~/.config/starship.toml Owns starship.toml, the same file on every OS (ANSI colors follow the theme) Git ~/.config/git/config defaults Moves those defaults into ~/.gitconfig and removes the XDG copy (its gh helper path is pinned to a mise version) Packages Base system (install/omarchy-base.packages) Installs apps.yaml linux: extras (Omarchy-shipped apps are omarchy: shipped) CLI tools pacman tools (bat, eza, fzf…) plus /etc/mise/conf.d/omarchy-tools.toml (gh, copilot, node, uv…) The mise config skips the pacman-shipped tools on Omarchy, and skips unpinned tools that Omarchy's mise config already declares (gh, copilot, codex, uv) Theme omarchy theme set Applies omarchyPrefs.theme when it changes Bar (omarchy/shell.json) Layout. Omarchy migrations rewrite it Merges in omarchyPrefs.bar only (see below) hypr/*.lua overrides Stock copies Omarchy never rewrites Not managed until you customize one (chezmoi add ~/.config/hypr/<file>) Hooks (omarchy/hooks/*.d) Hooks installed by Omarchy and plugins Not managed. Add your own with chezmoi add

Never edit or manage anything under /usr/share/omarchy.

docs.title: Preferences (.chezmoidata/omarchy.yaml)
docs.text:
omarchyPrefs:
  theme: Hackerman            # display name from `omarchy theme list`
  bar:
    elsewhenCities:           # world-clock cities, wherever the widget sits
      - { name: Chicago, zone: America/Chicago }
    tray:                     # plugin widgets, added only if the plugin is installed
      - superwhisper.panel
  • Theme: Linux/run_onchange_after_05-omarchy-theme.sh runs omarchy theme set only when this value changes. A theme picked in the switcher stays until you edit the file.
  • Bar: dot_config/omarchy/modify_shell.json.tmpl is a chezmoi modify script. It reads the current shell.json, sets the Elsewhen cities and appends missing tray plugins with jq, and leaves everything else as Omarchy wrote it. With no file, it starts from Omarchy's default.

docs.title: omarchy-refresh-config
docs.text: omarchy-refresh-config <path> copies an Omarchy default over ~/.config/<path> (it backs up the old file first). If that path is managed here, chezmoi diff shows the difference and chezmoi apply restores your version.

docs.title: Setting up a new Omarchy machine
docs.text:
1. Run the bootstrap one-liner from the README. It installs the Doppler CLI with mise and runs doppler login first, because templates read Doppler while they render.
  2. Answer the chezmoi init prompts.
  3. Review before applying: chezmoi diff --use-builtin-diff. The configured diff tool is code --wait, which opens VS Code.
  4. Run chezmoi apply. Expect sudo prompts for packages. The Steam and VS Code Omarchy installers launch the app when they finish.

docs.title: Other Linux distros
docs.text: The same repo works on plain Arch, Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora: packages come from the distro's managers (see Configuration), and the bash rc falls back to mise activate + starship init. The Omarchy-only parts (theme, bar, .config/hypr, .config/omarchy) are ignored.

docs.title: Automation Scripts (.chezmoiscripts)
docs.text:
Scripts are grouped by the OSes they run on. .chezmoiignore.tmpl hides every folder that doesn't apply to the current machine:

home/.chezmoiscripts/
├── Windows/   # windows only (PowerShell)
├── Darwin/    # macOS only (Homebrew)
├── Linux/     # Linux only (distro package managers, Omarchy)
└── posix/     # macOS + Linux (shared bash scripts)

Naming follows {run_type}_{sequence}-{name}.{ext}[.tmpl]. chezmoi runs the scripts in name order, so the numeric prefix controls ordering. A script that renders to nothing but whitespace is skipped. The work-only clone scripts use this to skip themselves unless workComputer or setupWork is true.

docs.title: Script types
docs.text: Prefix Runs run_ every chezmoi apply run_once_ once per unique script content run_onchange_ whenever the rendered content changes (scripts embed a hash of the data they read) …_before_ / …_after_ before / after files are written

docs.title: Windows/
docs.text:
• run_once_before_01-install-package-manager.ps1.tmpl: winget/choco bootstrap
  • run_02-install-apps.ps1.tmpl: installs and upgrades apps.yaml windows: entries
  • run_03-setup-vscode-profiles.ps1.tmpl: VS Code profile extension sync
  • run_onchange_after_03-mise-install.ps1.tmpl: mise install
  • run_after_04-sync-ai-tools.ps1.tmpl: see AI Tools
  • run_once_after_04-clone-{personal,work}-repos.ps1.tmpl
  • run_once_after_06-windows-setup.ps1.tmpl: debloat and OS settings

docs.title: Darwin/
docs.text:
• run_once_before_01-install-brew.sh: installs Homebrew
  • run_02-install-apps.sh.tmpl: brew update + brew upgrade, then brew bundle from apps.yaml darwin: entries

docs.title: Linux/
docs.text:
• run_02-install-apps.sh.tmpl: upgrades the system (omarchy update -y on Omarchy; pacman -Syu + AUR, apt-get upgrade or dnf upgrade elsewhere), then installs apps.yaml linux: entries with this distro's package managers (see Configuration). Pending upgrades and missing packages are checked without root, so sudo is only asked for when there is something to do.
  • run_onchange_after_05-omarchy-theme.sh.tmpl: Omarchy only, applies omarchyPrefs.theme (see Omarchy)

docs.title: posix/ (macOS + Linux)
docs.text:
• run_03-setup-vscode-profiles.sh.tmpl: VS Code profile extension sync. It reads JSON with jq, falling back to plutil.
  • run_onchange_after_03-mise-install.sh.tmpl: mise install
  • run_after_04-sync-ai-tools.sh.tmpl: see AI Tools
  • run_once_after_04-clone-{personal,work}-repos.sh.tmpl

docs.title: Same setup on every OS
docs.text:
Each OS runs the same steps: install and upgrade apps (02), sync VS Code profiles (03), mise install (03), sync AI tools (04), and clone repos (04). The clone scripts log gh in over https and clone into projectPath. Only these are OS-specific, because the OS needs them:

  • Package manager bootstrap: Chocolatey/WinGet on Windows, Homebrew on macOS (Linux uses the distro's own).
  • Windows/run_once_after_06-windows-setup: debloat and OS settings.
  • Linux/run_onchange_after_05-omarchy-theme: Omarchy only.

On Windows, only the package-manager, install-apps and Windows-setup scripts elevate. Everything that writes to your profile (VS Code extensions, mise tools, AI tools, cloned repos) runs as you, because files an elevated process creates are owned by Administrators.

Warning

The VS Code sync has REMOVE_EXTRA=true, so it uninstalls extensions that aren't declared in vscode-profiles.yaml.

docs.title: Adding a script
docs.text: Put it in the folder for the OSes it should run on. Use posix/ for bash that works on both macOS and Linux. Scripts that need mise tools should include {{ template "mise-path" . }}, because chezmoi's environment has no rc file loaded.

docs.title: Templates (.chezmoitemplates)
docs.text:
Chezmoi templates allow dynamic generation of files using:

  • Go template syntax
  • Functions provided by chezmoi
  • Custom helper functions defined in template files
  • Data from .chezmoidata/*

docs.title: Template Directory Structure
docs.text:
home/.chezmoitemplates/
├── ai-targets              # AI tools: does this entry target this agent?
├── elevate-powershell      # re-launch a PowerShell script as Administrator
├── is-omarchy              # "true" on Omarchy, empty elsewhere
├── mcp-server-json         # AI tools: MCP config as JSON
├── mcp-server-toml         # AI tools: MCP config as a Codex TOML table
├── mcp-server-toml-value
├── mise-path               # put mise tools on PATH inside chezmoi scripts
├── project-path            # projectPath with a leading ~ expanded
├── theme-helpers           # rgbToHex / rgbToFloat
├── vscode-keybindings
├── vscode-mcp
└── vscode-settings

Each file defines a reusable template fragment or function.

docs.title: is-omarchy
docs.text:
Prints true on Omarchy and nothing elsewhere. It is built on chezmoi's own data (.chezmoi.os, then .chezmoi.osRelease.id), so it is safe on Windows/macOS, where .chezmoi.osRelease doesn't exist.

{{ if includeTemplate "is-omarchy" . }}...{{ end }}

docs.title: project-path
docs.text:
Prints projectPath with a leading ~ expanded to the home directory. Neither bash nor PowerShell expands ~ inside quotes or when passing it to gh, so scripts use this instead of .projectPath:

PROJECT_PATH="{{ includeTemplate "project-path" . }}/Personal"

docs.title: mise-path
docs.text:
Scripts run without any shell rc file, so they can't see mise tools by default. This puts the mise shims on PATH (on macOS it loads Homebrew first, on Windows it re-reads PATH from the registry). Include it at the top of any script that calls a mise-managed tool:

{{ template "mise-path" . }}

docs.title: theme-helpers
docs.text: Defines rgbToHex and rgbToFloat for the colors in .chezmoidata/themes.yaml.

docs.title: vscode-settings and vscode-keybindings
docs.text:
These templates unify:

  • Shared base settings
  • Per-profile settings
  • OS-specific overrides

Used to generate:

  • ~/AppData/Roaming/Code/User/{settings,keybindings}.json (Windows)
  • ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/{settings,keybindings}.json (macOS)

docs.title: vscode-mcp
docs.text: Generates the VS Code user mcp.json (next to settings.json) from .chezmoidata/ai-tools.yaml — the MCP servers targeting any agent whose ai-agents.yaml mcp.method is vscode-json (Copilot today). VS Code requires MCP config in this dedicated file, not inside settings.json.

docs.title: mcp-server-json / mcp-server-toml / ai-targets
docs.text: Helpers for the AI tools sync. mcp-server-json renders an MCP config: as JSON (resolving {{ ... }} secrets); mcp-server-toml renders the same config as a Codex [mcp_servers.<name>] table; ai-targets answers "does this ai-tools.yaml entry target this agent?" and rejects agent names ai-agents.yaml doesn't define.

docs.title: elevate-powershell
docs.text: Contains logic for running elevated (Administrator) PowerShell tasks during script execution.

docs.title: Using Templates
docs.text:
Any file ending in .tmpl under home/ is treated as a template.

You can call templates using:

{{ template "vscode-settings" . }}

docs.title: Creating New Templates
docs.text: Templates are ideal for: - OS-specific file content - Reused settings (e.g., proxies, secrets prompts) - Shared JSON/YAML structures - Re-usable helper functions (math, strings, color transforms)

docs.title: Theme System
docs.text:
There are two theme systems, one per platform family:

  • Windows / macOS (VS Code): home/.chezmoidata/themes.yaml plus the theme-helpers template, selected by the .theme prompt.
  • Omarchy: Omarchy's own themes (omarchy theme list), selected by omarchyPrefs.theme in home/.chezmoidata/omarchy.yaml. See Omarchy. Omarchy already re-themes VS Code, terminals and the bar when the theme changes.

The Starship prompt (~/.config/starship.toml) only uses ANSI colors, so it follows whichever terminal theme is active on every OS.

docs.title: themes.yaml
docs.text:
Each theme (dracular, molokai, mojave_dark) defines background and foreground as [R, G, B] arrays, plus the 16 terminal colors as hex strings without # (d_* normal, l_* light/bright):

themes:
  dracular:
    background: [40, 42, 54]
    foreground: [248, 248, 242]
    d_red: [255, 85, 85]
    d_blue: BD93F9
    l_blue: CAA9FA
    # ...

docs.title: theme-helpers template
docs.text:
Defines two named templates for the RGB arrays:

  • rgbToHex: [R,G,B] to #RRGGBB
  • rgbToFloat: [R,G,B] to [r, g, b] floats from 0 to 1 (iTerm2 format)

docs.title: Using a theme in a template
docs.text:
{{- template "theme-helpers" -}}
{{- $themeColors := index .themes .theme -}}
"editor.background": "{{ template "rgbToHex" $themeColors.background }}",
"terminal.ansiBlue": "#{{ $themeColors.d_blue }}",

Note

Current state: no template uses these colors yet. vscode-settings looks up $themeColors but never reads it, and nothing calls theme-helpers. The .theme prompt (promptChoice in .chezmoi.json.tmpl, offering dracular / molokai) is asked on every chezmoi init. Either wire the colors into VS Code / Windows Terminal or remove themes.yaml, theme-helpers and the prompt.

docs.title: Visual Studio Code Integration
docs.text:
VS Code setup in this dotfiles repo is fully automated and templated, including:

  • settings
  • keybindings
  • extensions
  • profiles
  • OS-specific variations

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
home/
└── AppData/Roaming/Code/User/
├── settings.json.tmpl
└── keybindings.json.tmpl

home/.chezmoitemplates/
├── vscode-settings
└── vscode-keybindings

home/.chezmoidata/
└── vscode-profiles.yaml

docs.title: How Settings Are Generated
docs.text:
1. A shared base settings file is defined inside: 
    .chezmoitemplates/vscode-settings
  2. Additional configurations can be layered via:
  3. per-profile settings
  4. OS-specific checks
  5. theme colors

Example template:

{
    "editor.fontFamily": "JetBrains Mono",
    "workbench.colorCustomizations": {
        "activityBar.background": "{{ themeColor "primary" }}"
    }
}

docs.title: Extensions Installation
docs.text:
Extensions are declared in:

home/vscode-extensions.txt
Installed via: - macOS: run_onchange_03-install-vscode-extensions.sh.tmpl - Windows: run_onchange_03-install-vscode-extensions.ps1.tmpl

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Once vscode-profiles.yaml is added, you’ll be able to: - generate per-profile folders - merge base + profile settings - auto-install profile-specific extensions
